newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan wants to improve ties with Palau.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan wants to improve ties with Palau.

text.p: Taiwan's vice-president Lien Chan on Saturday expressed the government's desire to improve relations with Micronesian resort island Palau and said the future between the two nations was bright.

Lien, who doubles as Taiwan's premier, told visiting Palau Minister of State Andres Uherbe Lau that Taiwan hoped for more "meaningful development" in bilateral relations, the state-funded Central News Agency quoted Lien as saying.
Foreign Minister John Chang said on Friday that both Taiwan and Palau were keen to promote bilateral ties but added they were still "waiting for a proper moment", the agency said.

Palau has no diplomatic relations with Taiwan or arch rival China but has warm business ties with Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party, which pledged in 1995 to invest US$8 million to build a six-story hotel in Palau.
China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and refuses to recognise any country having official relations with the island.
Palau is a self-governing republic with full United Nations membership.
